verdict: JPMorgan reported $21.2B of profit — flattered by a $4.6B one-off gain on its Visa shares; even without the one-offs, it earned $16.9B as trading and fees boomed.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: reported basis, vs a year ago

segments.name: Net interest income
segments.note: Interest earned on loans and securities, minus the interest paid on deposits and borrowings — the bank's core engine, up 10% on bigger loan and deposit balances.

segments.name: Noninterest revenue
segments.note: Fees, trading and asset-management income — up 47%, inflated by a $4.6B gain on Visa shares and $1.0B of equity-investment gains. Excluding those, it rose about 20%.

opex.name: Compensation expense
opex.note: Pay and benefits for the bank's workforce — its biggest cost.

opex.name: Technology, communications & equipment
opex.note: Technology, telecoms and equipment as the bank invests in AI and its platforms.

opex.name: Occupancy & other expense
opex.note: Branches and offices ($1,482M of occupancy) plus other general costs ($2,043M).

takeaways.title: The Visa gain is the headline
takeaways.text: A $4.6B net gain on Visa shares in Corporate, plus $1.0B of equity-investment gains, sits inside this quarter's revenue. Excluding significant items, net income was $16.9B ($6.14 a share) instead of $21.2B ($7.70).

takeaways.title: Returns no rival matches
takeaways.text: With the one-offs included, return on tangible common equity hit 29% — profitability far beyond what other big banks produce.

takeaways.title: Credit costs fell
takeaways.text: The provision for credit losses fell 12% from a year ago to $2.5B — $2.4B of actual charge-offs plus a small $149M reserve build — even as lending kept growing.

oneTimers: A $4.6B net gain related to Visa shares (in Corporate) and $1.0B of gains on certain equity investments ($763M of it in Corporate) are inside noninterest revenue. Excluding these significant items, net income was $16.9B and EPS $6.14 instead of $21.2B and $7.70.
follow100Note: JPMorgan reports revenue two ways: $57.3B reported (GAAP), used here, or $58.0B on a 'managed' basis that grosses up tax-exempt income. Net income is identical either way.
footerNote: JPMorgan headlines 'managed' revenue of $58.0B; this page uses reported (GAAP) revenue of $57.3B — the difference is a tax gross-up that does not change net income. For a bank, credit costs (the provision for credit losses) play the role of cost of revenue, and 'operating profit' here is income before income taxes.
